subject: Commit stabilizer & escrow clause — proposed resolution and next steps
messages:
From: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@orbiton-health.com>
To: jordan_blake@redwood.com
Cc: ken.oneal@orbiton-health.com
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on commit stabilizer / escrow proposal (Order Form v4)

Jordan — thanks for the call today. As we review the order form your team shared, two items remain blockers for procurement: the ‘Commit Stabilizer’ (pricing floor/collar) math and the proposed escrow/escrow-trigger mechanism tied to a quarterly true-up. Our finance team is comfortable with a collar-style minimum but needs (1) clearer language on when the escrow releases, and (2) a cap on potential clawbacks so Orbiton’s cash forecasting isn’t exposed to open-ended refund risk.

Attached is a lightly annotated redline (ORB_OrderForm_v4_redline.pdf) from our procurement lead that shows the escrow trigger tied to a surprise churn metric. That’s the piece we want to avoid. Can Redwood propose an alternative that limits our exposure to a maximum repayment equal to one quarter’s committed spend and ties release to a standard three-step reconciliation (monthly usage report, 15-day dispute window, autopay adjustment)?

Appreciate a short write-up and a clean order form we can take to our CFO next week.

— Marta
Procurement Lead, Orbiton Health
(attachment: ORB_OrderForm_v4_redline.pdf)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Questions on commit stabilizer / escrow proposal (Order Form v4)

Marta — thanks for the clear notes and the redline. I’ve looped in Ben (AE) and Karthik (Legal) to help us land language that meets Orbiton’s forecasting needs while keeping Redwood’s servicing economics intact.

Quick proposal to accelerate: Redwood can (a) limit total clawback exposure to 25% of the quarter commit (we're open to converting to a fixed cap equal to one quarter’s committed spend if that’s preferable), (b) move the escrow release to a three-step reconciliation you suggested (monthly usage report, 15-day dispute window, automatic adjustment), and (c) replace the ‘surprise churn’ trigger with a defined set of exceptions (force majeure, catastrophic regional outage) so there’s no surprise clawback for routine variability.

We’ll draft updated language and a short escrow worksheet so your finance team can see the math. Attaching the current draft we’ll edit (Redwood_OrderForm_draft_v3.pdf) and will produce an escrow schedule spreadsheet for transparency.

— Jordan
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Greg Palmer <gpalmer@mercerlaw.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Cc: marta.ruiz@orbiton-health.com, ken.oneal@orbiton-health.com
Date: Sat, 3 Oct 2026 11:36:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: ORB OrderForm v4 — redline + escrow math

Folks — forwarding Orbiton’s redline with counsel comments. Two notes from our side: Orbiton’s request to cap clawbacks at one quarter’s committed spend is typical; however the escrow construction needs clarity on timing and source of funds. If Redwood intends to hold an escrow funded from prepayments, we should state the funding mechanism, who controls the escrow account, and an irrevocable payment trigger only after the dispute window closes.

I’ve attached a marked-up clause and a suggested escrow schedule. The suggested mechanics:
- Escrow funded monthly from 20% of overage collections until a target cap is reached.
- Release tied to the three-step reconciliation (monthly report + 15-day dispute + automated adjustment).
- Maximum clawback equals the lesser of (a) one quarter committed spend, or (b) amount held in escrow.

If Redwood prefers a warranty-style clawback (return funds after an audit) vs. escrow, call that out so we can evaluate.

— Greg (outside counsel)
(attachment: ORB_OrderForm_v4_redline.pdf [forwarded])

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Greg Palmer <gpalmer@mercerlaw.com>, marta.ruiz@orbiton-health.com
Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 5 Oct 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ORB OrderForm v4 — proposed escrow & cap language

Greg / Marta / team — thanks for the redline and the practical suggestions. We reviewed internally (legal + finance) and propose the following compromise language for the Order Form:

"Escrow; Clawback Cap. Customer and Redwood agree to an escrow arrangement to hold amounts related to usage true-ups where Customer has pre-paid committed spend. Redwood will fund the escrow from excess prepayments or overage collections; Redwood will not seek additional cash from Customer to fund the escrow. The escrow will be released to Customer subject to a three-step reconciliation process: (i) Redwood provides Customer with a detailed monthly usage report within 10 business days following the month; (ii) Customer has 15 calendar days to notify Redwood of any disputes to the report; and (iii) absent a timely dispute Redwood will issue an automatic credit to Customer's account and release the escrowed funds to Customer within 30 business days.

Notwithstanding the foregoing, Redwood's maximum aggregate clawback liability under this Order Form shall be capped at the lesser of (A) the total amount then held in escrow and (B) the Customer's committed spend for the applicable quarter. For the avoidance of doubt, routine usage fluctuation shall not trigger clawback events; clawback mechanics apply only when a final true-up following the three-step reconciliation results in a net credit due to Customer. Escrow funds shall be held in a segregated account maintained by Redwood or a mutually agreed third-party escrow agent and shall be subject to audit by Customer no more than once per rolling 12-month period upon reasonable notice."

We believe this language addresses Orbiton’s cash forecasting concern (explicit cap and release timing), avoids Redwood taking on open-ended exposures, and ties clawback to a transparent reconciliation flow. We are open to replacing the phrase "lesser of" with a fixed numeric cap equal to one quarter’s committed spend if Orbiton prefers simpler math — happy to insert exact values for the Order Form once you confirm the quarter commit figure.

Also attaching a simple escrow worksheet (Redwood_Escrow_Schedule_20261005.xlsx) that models a 25% cap vs. a fixed one-quarter cap so finance can compare.

— Karthik
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
(attachment: Redwood_Escrow_Schedule_20261005.xlsx)
